title: Attain the sharp Gaussian rounding budget at exact least period
body:
## Result

**Scoped proof.** An exact-sum Gaussian-pair rounder with Euclidean error at most one can have finite global least period `m` exactly when `4` divides `m`. Its sharp outward norm slack is

```text
sqrt((R^2+2R+3)/2) - sqrt((R^2+1)/2)
```

where `R` is the least odd integer at least five that does not divide `m`. The proof joins `m/4` four-cycles in the sum-one fiber into one cycle of length `m). Alternating the switches between opposite sides of adjacent rings keeps all new edges at error one. The chosen position places their absolute radial changes below the sharp bound. At exact period eight the optimum is `sqrt(19)-sqrt(13)`.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Ali Romman's #7714 at `ba5e006ed70119b23d6ef9e2e8627e43a3f4f18b` supplies the lower bound and starting map. Jerry Chen's #7570 supplies the annular matching, and Ali Romman's #7699 and #6509 supply the ring lower-bound framework and the Gaussian transform. [Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19718444)

## Evidence and reproduction

Both verifier modes checked 20 orbits through period 13,860, 16,940 Gaussian edges, 8,430 switched successors and four controls. Each registered command took under 0.1 seconds locally on macOS arm64. The written proof covers all admissible periods.

Run from the repository root with CPython 3.12.15 and the standard library.

```sh
pkg=research/gaussian-rounder-exact-period
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package "$pkg"
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package "$pkg" --check-source-history
python3.12 -I -W error -B "$pkg/verify.py"
python3.12 -I -W error -O -B "$pkg/verify.py"
```

The two verifier modes print `PASS_GAUSSIAN_ROUNDER_EXACT_PERIOD`. The metadata and commit preflight print `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limitations

The proof uses the iterate theorem as a cited premise. The predecessor replays, selected cold replay, Lean, Docker and physical caller checks were unrun. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Physical caller admission, tape and stock pricing and any change to κ remain open.

## Open next questions

Identify a physical caller that requires a prescribed least period. The first step is to specify its row and address schedule before pricing the splice predicate, coordinate arithmetic and workspace restoration.

## Related open work

- #7714 proves the sharp budget for the iterate identity and supplies both premises for this exact-period extension.
- #7699 gives the forced ring classification and the fourth-power budget. The new result attains that same budget at exact period four.
- #7570 gives the square-to-wire-swap optimum, equal to the new exact-period-four value.
- #7696 studies unrestricted period at the sharp radial threshold.
- #7698 supplies port and covariance contracts for the unrestricted sharp rounder.
- #7673 gives a forward-only lower bound without a finite-period requirement.
- #7652 gives a finite Hall lower bound for injective exact-sum rounding without a period requirement.
- #7572 analyzes the slack of affine-period and bounded-center families.
- #7569 gives an optimum for the larger class of Gaussian-pair rounders without the conserved-sum constraint.
- #7651 gives finite-radius thresholds for a larger Gaussian rounding domain without the conserved-sum constraint.

## CI notes

The registered normal and optimized replays and the committed-byte/source-history preflight passed locally. Hosted CI is pending.
